## Keep wall ghosts consistent with the hydrostatic reference (`dynamics/wb-wall-clamp`) {#sec-ch11-wb}

### Summary

The well-balanced x1 reconstruction of @sec-ch05 subtracts a discretely hydrostatic reference from pressure
and density, reconstructs only the perturbations, and restores the reference at the faces. Near a wall two
things must be decided: how the reference itself continues into the ghosts, since its five-point smoothing
reads two cells past every owned cell, and what perturbation the ghosts carry. This scheme states both
decisions and the different face predicates they use: the continuation is gated on a physical face, the
mirror on a physical face that is not outflow.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Continue the wall reference; @eq-ch11-wb-continuation.

**Data.** Cell-average density/pressure ratio and reference perturbations.

**Placement.** Gravity-driven well-balanced x1 reconstruction.

**Activation.** `dynamics/wb-wall-clamp: true` by default; mirror has no switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Smooth uniform-grid truncation argument; solver order unmeasured.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

All states here are cell averages; $\chi=\rho/p$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,m^{-2}}$.
Write the default reference smoothing with the notation-table binomial weights $B=(1,4,6,4,1)/16$.
On a uniform grid its unit sum and zero first moment reproduce linear data. Repeating the first owned
$\chi$[^rg-4b8844d07ce3] beyond a wall breaks that cancellation: a Taylor expansion has an uncancelled first-derivative term
of order $h$. Continuing from two owned cells cancels it.

Let owned cells start at index zero, let $l$ count continuation depth, and use positive owned values.
The implementation chooses

$$
\chi_{-l}=\begin{cases}
\chi_0(\chi_0/\chi_1)^l,&\chi_1>\chi_0,\\
\chi_0+l(\chi_0-\chi_1),&\chi_1\le\chi_0.
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch11-wb-continuation}

`hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop >}}) implements
@eq-ch11-wb-continuation, with fallback to $\chi_0$ if the computed value is not positive, and
`hydro_ref_x1_rop_smooth` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h hydro_ref_x1_rop_smooth >}}) calls it for
the stencil points past a clamped end and repeats the wall cell when the end is not clamped. The first branch
linearly continues $\log\chi$, the second $\chi$. Expanding the power branch about equal adjacent values
gives the same constant and linear terms as the second branch; the difference is $O(h^2)$ at fixed $l$. The
binomial first moment then cancels the wall's $O(h)$ error for smooth data on a uniform grid. This is a
truncation argument, not a fitted solver order. The reference construction is derived in @sec-ch05; the
underlying note is `docs/derivations/wb-ref-wall.md@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` section 4. No
measured values from that note are reused. Check C7 checks the binomial moments, the repeated-cell linear
bias and the first-order agreement of the two continuations symbolically.

The sweep subtracts $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$[^rg-782303cf9534], then mirrors the perturbations:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p'_{i-l}&=p'_{i+l-1},\\
\rho'_{i-l}&=\rho'_{i+l-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-wb-parity}

The well-balanced branch of `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}})
implements @eq-ch11-wb-parity with a `flip` of the first (last) $n_g$ owned perturbations into the ghosts,
guarded by `is_outflow` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp is_outflow >}}) so that it acts only at physical
non-outflow faces. If the cell state matches the discrete reference exactly, both perturbations vanish,
their mirrors vanish, and a constant-preserving reconstruction returns zero perturbation. Restoring matched
reference face values therefore adds no perturbation flux residual. The full pressure/gravity cancellation
is the well-balanced scheme's identity, not a consequence of parity alone. Check C7 checks the
zero-perturbation preservation [check `src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The well-balanced x1 path engages when $g_1\ne0$, the state carries a pressure row and the EOS is not
shallow water; an older isentropic ghost revision at the walls is present only as commented-out code.
`HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}) passes two flags
to the reference kernel, one per x1 end, each true when that face is physical and `wb_wall_clamp` is on;
unlike the perturbation mirror, these flags do not exclude an outflow face. The continuation needs two
owned cells next to the wall; a block too thin for that is the reference kernel's own case and is covered
by its tests. The optional mass-covariance path (`SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE`, default off, read once by
`HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance >}}) uses
one-sided second-order density derivatives in the first and last cell and an odd mirror of the corrected
velocity, at the same physical non-outflow ends. Without the well-balanced path, the gravity branch
reconstructs the full state and revises the reconstructed face pairs at the physical ends instead
(`_revise_x1inner_lr`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_lr >}}).

The fourth-order reference variant is selected by `SNAP_WB_REF4` (`wb_ref4_enabled`,
{{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}), which `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (`x1_centroid_exact_enabled`,
{{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}) implies; both environment switches default
off, and the variant builds its stencils with the same clamp-and-physical flags. This section does not
rederive their high-order stencils (@sec-ch05) or assign measured wall or seam convergence to them.

@fig-ch11-wb-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

### Code

**How to use.** Add this fragment to a complete stratified deck with nonzero x1 gravity and a pressure-bearing EOS
other than shallow water. The flag alone does not activate well-balanced reconstruction. The perturbation mirror
has no separate YAML key.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dynamics`[^rg-ab31b442efcd], `wb-wall-clamp`[^rg-3049dc326e45].
```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: reflecting
    x1-outer: reflecting
dynamics:
  wb-wall-clamp: true
```

**Refusals and prerequisites.** The continuation helper does not throw for a nonpositive candidate: it falls back
to the nearest owned ratio. Unknown dynamics keys are refused by the options parser. The clamp uses physical-face
flags; the perturbation mirror additionally excludes outflow.

**Read the implementation.** `hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop >}}) contains:

```cpp
T e = r1 > r0 ? r0 * pow(r0 / r1, T(k)) : r0 + T(k) * (r0 - r1);
return e > T(0) ? e : r0;
```

`r0`, `r1` and `k` denote $\chi_0$, $\chi_1$ and continuation depth in @eq-ch11-wb-continuation. The conditional selects its two branches; the return implements the positive-value fallback.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| wboption | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `wb_wall_clamp` | `dynamics/wb-wall-clamp` |
| wbflags | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `wb_x1` | none |
| wb | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `is_outflow` | none |
| masscov | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::x1_mass_covariance >}} | `x1_mass_covariance` | `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` |
| nonwb | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_lr >}} | `_revise_x1inner_lr` | none |
| ref | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}} | `wall_clamp` | `dynamics/wb-wall-clamp` |
| wallrop | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop >}} | `hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop` | `dynamics/wb-wall-clamp` |

: Implementation sites for wb. {#tbl-ch11-wb-code}

1. Select the gravity/pressure well-balanced branch and build its reference with the physical-face clamp
   flags. The anchor `wall_clamp` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}.
2. Subtract the reference and mirror the perturbations only at physical non-outflow ends. The anchor
   `is_outflow` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
3. Apply the selected mass-covariance wall treatment, reconstruct the perturbations, and restore the
   reference at the faces; the non-WB[^rg-1f7dbd3c21f3] path revises the face pairs instead. The anchor `_revise_x1inner_lr`
   is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_lr >}}.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wb_ref_wall.release` | The reference and reconstructed densities at the faces next to the walls converge at second order between two grids | two-grid slope at least $1.7$ | test constant |
| `test_hydro_ref_x1.release` | With the clamp, changed ghost values leave the interior reference unchanged; without it they do not | exact equality; inequality on the off arm | test assertions |
| `boundary_check.py` (report only) | `[C7]` as described below | exact | symbolic, rational or integer identity |

The clamp assertions are in
{{< code tests/test_hydro_ref_x1.cpp HydroRefX1Dispatch.wall_clamp_keeps_the_interior_free_of_the_ghosts >}}
and {{< code tests/test_hydro_ref_x1.cpp HydroRefX1Dispatch.without_the_clamp_the_ghosts_do_reach_the_interior >}}.

**Not provided:** a round-off derivation for each tolerance, because the cited tests give acceptance
criteria without deriving each round-off bound, and this book does not derive those bounds.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

The report-only checks `[C7]` establish that the binomial moments are (1, 0, 1), the repeated-wall linear bias is
3/8 and the continuation residuals vanish.[^ch11-wb-run]
These checks exercise report formulas, not the compiled boundary kernels. The source-test table records
assertions and tolerances, not new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver results.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The reference clamp still receives the physical-face flags for an outflow face
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}); it is incorrect to summarize all wall
operations of this scheme as excluding outflow. An in-block periodic x1 callback counts as physical here
while `is_x1_wall` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::is_x1_wall >}}) excludes its name. The
two-resolution test assertion is not the three-resolution fitted order the report requires for a
measurement. Nonuniform-grid wall accuracy and the outflow/implicit/WB combinations are unmeasured. The
derivation is restricted to smooth uniform-grid data.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
